title: Macro Overuse for Trivial Getter Generation (Obscuring Code Navigation)
pattern: Writing custom preprocessor macros to eliminate trivial boilerplate code like simple accessors or field setters.
why_bad: It makes code navigation and IDE "Go to Definition" completely impossible. Compiler warning messages inside macro expansions are notoriously difficult to understand, rendering code review highly challenging.
detection: Use of custom declarative or procedural macros to declare individual public methods on domain structures.
counterexample: Standard widely-accepted macro crates (like `serde` or standard library `#[derive(Clone)]`) where the generated code obeys structural standards.
source: *Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 8 (Macros) / *The Pragmatic Programmer*, Topic Kaizen.
